references.text: The context where Judas's men came to bind Samson and hand him over to the Philistines, which directly leads to this verse.
Samson was bound again with new ropes, a recurring theme of attempts to bind him.
The Philistines finally captured Samson and bound him, contrasting with his earlier ability to break bonds.
David swore not to kill Saul, similar to the promise here not to kill Samson.
Jesus was bound and handed over to the authorities, parallel to Samson being bound and handed over to the Philistines.
Jesus was bound and led away, a similar motif of a strong person voluntarily allowing himself to be bound.
